rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Protista holds the eukaryotes that are neither plants, animals nor fungi — mostly single-celled aquatic organisms. Protozoa, their animal-like members, are classified by locomotion: Rhizopoda creep on pseudopodia (Amoeba), Mastigophora swim on flagella (Trypanosoma), Ciliophora row on cilia with two nuclei (Paramecium), and Sporozoa glide as non-motile obligate parasites with complex life cycles (Plasmodium).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Rhizopoda pseudopodia, Flagellata flagella, Ciliata cilia, Sporozoa none.
Ciliate nuclei: macronucleus for vegetative control, micronucleus for genetic exchange.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Pseudopodia vs cilia vs flagella:** pseudopodia are flowing cell extensions (Rhizopoda); cilia are many short oars (Ciliophora); flagella are few long whips (Mastigophora).  ·  **Protista vs Monera:** protists are eukaryotic with a true nucleus; Monera are prokaryotic.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Class names have older synonyms: Sarcodina for Rhizopoda, Mastigophora for Flagellata. Either pair is acceptable if the example matches.  ·  Do not invent extra classes. These four cover the course.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Amoeba proteus*** — rhizopod moving by pseudopodia.  ·  ***Paramecium caudatum*** — ciliate with macro- and micronucleus.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Classification questions expect class name + locomotor organ + example — all three together.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Make the four-row classification table.  ·  List holozoic, saprozoic, parasitic and mixotrophic with one organism each.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Pseudopodia, Flagella, Cilia, None — Rhizopoda, Mastigophora, Ciliophora, Sporozoa."

rows.label: Board question

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Locomotion classifies protozoa:** the four classes are distinguished chiefly by their locomotor organelle — pseudopodia, flagella, cilia or none.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Protista: eukaryotic, mostly unicellular, aquatic; autotrophic or heterotrophic.  ·  Protozoa classes: Rhizopoda (pseudopodia — Amoeba), Mastigophora (flagella — Trypanosoma), Ciliophora (cilia, two nuclei — Paramecium), Sporozoa (non-motile parasites — Plasmodium).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Protozoa were among the first eukaryotes to evolve, over a billion years before multicellular animals.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Amoeba is placed in → B  ·  Paramecium moves by → B
